Variants.Content: Tuk is the home in the Iban cultural circle. In addition to whaling, Iban’s furs, wood, fish and whale products must be collected, preserved and transported by sea in exchange for food, metal and southern goods; Tuk’s living space lies in this chain. It needed to get inland hunters, port warehouse owners, captains, and outside traders to accept the same set of weights and credits. It also had to prevent a single port closure from depleting reserves. The family can adjust its focus between trade and military affairs, but if the island's dependence on imported food and safe shipping routes is forgotten, no matter how rich the warehouse is, it will become an empty name in the cold season.

When Iban merchants look at Tuk, they pay attention to whether the scales are consistent and whether old debts are acknowledged. The northern voyage is dangerous enough, and no one wants to hand over goods to someone who will change their story after landing.

Orions and craftsmen hope that Tuke will give a purchase price that can allow people to survive, and they also hate merchants hoarding when the price of foreign grains increases. The cold winter magnifies every injustice.

The captain and the guards believed that Took needed both profit and money for convoys, lights, and dock maintenance. A family that only uses a port without providing for it will not be respected for a long time.
